title: Prospective decision coverage across two prediction tracks
scope: Aggregate author analysis of two AlphaGenome output tracks. GM12878 discovery and new-locus replication are distinct cohorts; paired IMR-90 reuses the 84 replication sites and model architecture. Clinical-credit comparisons in replication and portability are descriptive.

cohorts.label: Paired IMR-90 test
cohorts.scope_note: Same 84 replication sites; second track within one model.

findings: Locked IMR-90 predictions identified 49/84 centered leaders versus 7/84 with simple bounds: 42 additional decisions across six genes, no observed contradictions, and 35 unresolved sites.
Universal endpoint saturation did not transfer: 249/252 IMR-90 comparisons saturated. Both bounds abstained at the three exceptional sites; the witness-specific gain occurred elsewhere.
All 612 GM12878 comparisons numerically saturated. Centering resolved 138/141 native ties and preserved all 63 strict native leaders across discovery and replication.
Selected-allele credit decreased after centering in GM12878 replication and increased in IMR-90. RMS map baselines exceeded centered H1 credit in both tracks. No clinical superiority is established.
No discovery main or sensitivity test survived Holm adjustment over all sixteen tests. No new confirmatory clinical-enrichment family was added.

A targeted Julia/Ripserer check reproduced all 72 full diagrams (847,288 intervals) from nine selected replication sites on both tracks, including all known IMR-90 exceptions. This is separate-implementation agreement on identical effective float32 inputs, not full-cohort or independent-model validation.
limits: One model, two output tracks; paired IMR-90 reuses the seven replication loci rather than adding independent sites.
Native-only bounds predict the centered endpoint. Two-endpoint envelopes audit the full path after both distances are available.
Selected sites, overlapping within-gene windows and clinically ascertained labels limit generalization.
Practical numerical allowances are not formal real-arithmetic certificates; no measured runtime advantage is claimed.
These are model predictions, not experimentally validated chromatin changes or calibrated clinical predictions.
